label: Mark van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism vs §5.2…: Anti-realism: moral propositions, properties and…
locator: §5.2, 'According to anti-realist theories, entities or properties such as proposition, property, truth, truth conditions, and representation are explained by our use of terms for them in our thought and talk.'
interpretation: Dreier (2018): the distinction between realism and anti-realism (non-cognitivism, relativism) is one of order of explanation. Read as the quasi-realist's answer to an explanatory-order question (does moral practice explain moral truth, or the reverse?), not as an account of what makes a particular moral judgment true (Codex P1 on #189). Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
